newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Court transfers Bhutto's husband to jail.
newsitem.headline: Court transfers Bhutto's husband to jail.

text.p: A Pakistan court on Thursday transferred Asif Ali Zardari, husband of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, to jail from police custody after he complained of "mental torture" while in police hands.
"Zardari has been given the jail custody instead of police custody," lawyer Farooq Naek told Reuters. An accused prisoner cannot be interrogated while in jail custody, legal sources said.

Naek said judicial magistrate Rashida Siddiqui had ordered that Zardari be remanded to jail until January 2 instead of police custody. Naek said his client had been interrogated by government agencies other than police.

Despite an earlier court order that Zardari should be interrogated only by an investigating officer, personnel from other agencies were interrogating him at various times of the day, Naek said. "He is suffering mental torture as he is not allowed to sleep properly," the lawyer added.

Zardari was re-arrested on December 19 on suspicion of involvement in the alleged murder of Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza. Earlier he had been released from a Karachi jail when a court declared his six-week detention illegal.
On Saturday, Zardari told the magistrate that he had been falsely implicated in the killing of a person he had always respected, and that he feared police would poison his food.

Murtaza's Lebanese-born widow Ghinwa, now chief of a breakaway faction of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party, has accused Zardari, former home minister Naseerullah Babar, former Sindh province chief minister Abdullah Shah and police of conspiring in the September 20 killing of her husband in a shootout near his Karachi home.
Police say Murtaza was killed in crossfire after his bodyguards fired first at police.

A judicial tribunal is already investigating the incident, which Benazir says was a conspiracy against her family and government, sacked on November 5 by President Leghari on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Bhutto and Zardari have been at the centre of corruption allegations associated with the former government. Both deny any wrongdoing.
